authorization.scope: User approved implementation of retained SQLite connection, coalesced progress saving and readable export. Subsequent instructions selected a 30-second default with early saves on background/close and requested a five-choice 5/10/15/30/60 second Settings slider.

implementation.connection: One application-managed Mutex<Connection>, initialized in Tauri setup and reused by existing blocking commands; progress statements are prepared and cached.
implementation.scheduling: Latest dirty anchor per book; one non-resetting timer; elapsed monotonic time survives interval changes; acknowledged unchanged positions do not write; failed IPC outcomes invalidate earlier acknowledgements.
implementation.settings: Five discrete slider positions in seconds, default 30; retained through the existing webview localStorage preference convention, with default/session fallback on unavailable storage.
implementation.lifecycle: Shelf return, hidden visibility, pagehide and desktop focus loss request early saving. Normal close prevents native destruction until pending progress succeeds; errors or an active book operation retain the window. Late subscriptions and replaced views are disposed.
implementation.export: On-demand version-1 saga-library-state JSON contains catalog metadata, progress, timestamps and retained review fingerprints. Snapshot reads use one SQLite read transaction. A selected destination is replaced through a synced sibling staging file after releasing the database connection. It does not include book bodies or UI preferences and has no restore/import interface.

verification.sampleTests: Two SAGA_SAMPLE-dependent original-book checks remain ignored; ordinary tests use isolated fixtures.

performance.scope: Isolated implemented storage-call path; excludes Tauri IPC, UI rendering, complete application startup, mobile energy and cold-cache behavior.
performance.method: Both paths use 1000 synthetic book rows and WAL synchronous=NORMAL. Three trials alternate method order. Each trial updates one active book 3000 times. Baseline compiles the pre-change storage source from the retained snapshot; implemented compiles the current Database::execute plus storage::update_progress, including mutex, input validation and cached statement. Batch totals include automatic checkpoints and explicitly account for final checkpoint/close. Every case verifies the final anchor after closing/reopening.
limits: Shared Windows host, warm synthetic data and reused dependency artifacts; this is local diagnostic evidence, not a qualified performance budget.
The harness leaves the engine default automatic checkpoint threshold unchanged; it is not a separate measurement of checkpoint scheduling.
No claim of equivalent power-loss persistence, mobile battery savings or full application speedup.
Real desktop event delivery, normal-close UI interaction and native save-dialog interaction remain untested.
Forced process termination, operating-system shutdown and power loss are not covered by close hooks; SQLite WAL/NORMAL durability semantics are unchanged.
Timer throttling, process suspension, busy storage and long archive operations can delay saving beyond the selected scheduling interval.
Existing .saga/catalog ordinary-failure rollback remains distinct from cross-resource crash recovery.
The host blocking-worker admission queue and end-to-end memory/latency are not bounded by this change.
Release qualification remains GAP-04; no commit, push, application start or live migration was performed.
